subject: general
question: The solute-like component or the dispersed particles in a colloid form the _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersed phase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **colloid** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which one substance of microscopically dispersed insoluble particles is suspended throughout another substance.
 
• The **solute-like component** or the **dispersed particles** in a colloid form the **dispersed phase**. It represents the **discontinuous phase** of the system.
 
• The component in which the **dispersed phase** is suspended is known as the **dispersing medium** (or **dispersion medium**). It is analogous to the **solvent** in a true solution and is also called the **continuous phase**.
 
• Colloidal particles have a size ranging between **1 nanometer (nm)** and **1000 nanometers (nm)**. They are large enough to scatter light but small enough to remain suspended without settling.
 
• While a **solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** where the solute completely dissolves in the solvent, a **colloid** remains **heterogeneous** even if it appears uniform to the naked eye.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Colloids:** Colloids are classified based on the state (**solid, liquid, or gas**) of the **dispersed phase** and the **dispersion medium**.

 
 
• **Aerosol:** **Liquid or solid** dispersed in **gas** (e.g., **fog, clouds, smoke**).
 
• **Foam:** **Gas** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **shaving cream, whipped cream**).
 
• **Emulsion:** **Liquid** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **milk, face cream, hair cream**).
 
• **Sol:** **Solid** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **milk of magnesia, mud, paints**).
 
• **Gel:** **Liquid** dispersed in **solid** (e.g., **jelly, cheese, butter**).
 
 
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** This is the **scattering of a beam of light** by **colloidal particles**. Because the particles in the **dispersed phase** are large enough, they reflect light, making the path of the beam visible. This effect is not seen in **true solutions** because the solute particles are too small.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** Colloidal particles exhibit a **continuous zigzag motion** called **Brownian motion**. This movement is caused by the **unbalanced bombardment** of the particles of the **dispersed phase** by the molecules of the **dispersion medium**.
 
• **Stability:** Colloids are quite **stable**. Unlike **suspensions** (where particles are **greater than 1000 nm**), the particles in the **dispersed phase** of a colloid do not settle down when left undisturbed for a long period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solvent (Option 1):** This term is specifically used for **true solutions** (homogeneous mixtures) to describe the component present in the **larger amount** that dissolves the solute. In colloids, the equivalent term is the **dispersion medium**.
 
• **Continuous Phase (Option 3):** This is a synonym for the **dispersion medium**. It is the phase that surrounds the dispersed particles. Since the question asks for the "dispersed particles" component, this option is incorrect as it describes the medium instead.
 
• **Solution Phase (Option 4):** This is not a standard scientific term used to describe the internal components of a **colloidal system**. A **solution** consists of a **solute** and a **solvent** on a **molecular or ionic level**.
 
• **Dialysis:** It is a process used for **purifying colloids** by removing **electrolytes** or **crystalloids** through a **semi-permeable membrane**.
 
• **Electrophoresis:** The movement of **colloidal particles** under the influence of an **electric field**, which helps determine the **charge** (positive or negative) carried by the **dispersed phase** particles.
